1. Executive Summary

A snapshot of the June 2026 helpdesk picture: where users are getting stuck, which services are taking the heaviest hit, and what the highest-impact moves look like.

How users are getting stuck

Top 5 services by ticket volume

The five things leadership should know

  1. A regulatory event was June's biggest new ticket driver. The ADREC rental-increase freeze (announced 2–3 June) generated 132 tickets — clarification requests, non-compliance reports against landlords, and renewals blocked mid-flow. Publishing the rule inside the renewal flow would absorb most of this temporary demand.
  2. Users still cannot update their own information. Profile and company-detail updates (245 tickets) plus manual cancellations (149) and wallet corrections (20) keep self-service gaps as the #1 recurring product pain — 22.7% of analysable volume, unchanged in nature since April.
  3. When an action fails, users get no explanation. Submit / approve / pay / download failures with non-diagnostic errors are the single largest issue (269 tickets, 14.3%), now including output documents (receipts, broker cards) that silently fail to generate.
  4. The approve flow is a recurring hard blocker. Missing approve buttons and blank approval screens cluster in advertisement permits / Madhmoun; agencies report it "always happening". These 20 tickets block transactions outright and are growing vs May.
  5. Cross-system sync now leaks into visas and title deeds. Tenancy contracts not linked to ICP block family-visa applications; projects converted to Ready still show as Off-Plan and block title-deed registration. Backend sync remains the highest-leverage engineering investment.

8. Month over Month — May vs June 2026

Side-by-side comparison of the May and June datasets across volume, services, pain categories, top product issues, and confidence.
